subtopic: TVM / Operator fusion — graph-level and tensor-level
learningObjective: Distinguish graph-level operator fusion in Relax from loop-level fusion in TensorIR and understand what each achieves.
stem: Which statements about operator fusion in TVM are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Graph-level fusion in Relax groups multiple ops into a single fused sub-function (often a call into a fused PrimFunc), reducing kernel launch counts and enabling shared intermediate buffers.

Loop-level fusion in TensorIR (`sch.compute_inline`, `sch.reverse_compute_at`) merges producer and consumer loop nests inside a PrimFunc, eliminating intermediate materialization and improving locality.
Graph-level fusion can always fuse arbitrary op pairs; there is no notion of a fusion boundary or per-op fusion policy in Relax.
External-library ops (e.g., calls to cuBLAS or cuDNN) can be freely fused with generated PrimFunc kernels because Relax's fusion pass rewrites external calls into loop bodies at compile time.

explanation: A: Relax's graph-level fusion groups ops into a fused function/PrimFunc — this is the standard fusion optimization at the operator level, reducing launches and enabling scalar/tensor reuse. B: Loop-level fusion in TensorIR merges producer/consumer via `compute_inline` or `compute_at` primitives. C is wrong: Relax defines fusion patterns/policies (e.g., what op types can be epilogue-fused, per-op fusion attributes); not everything fuses. D is wrong: external-library calls are opaque black boxes; they cannot be rewritten into loop bodies and thus cannot participate in TensorIR-level fusion the same way generated PrimFuncs can.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: graph-level fusion at the Relax layer.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: loop-level fusion via TensorIR schedule primitives.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: Relax has fusion policies with defined boundaries.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: external ops are opaque and not rewritten into loops.

nonImplications: Does not imply graph-level and loop-level fusion are redundant; they operate at different scales and can compose.
Does not imply fusion always improves performance; over-fusion can hurt register/SMEM pressure.

distractorRationales.D: Confuses opaque external calls with generated PrimFuncs.

sourceRefs.locator: Fusion pass in Relax; TensorIR compute_inline / compute_at
